Class exercise to import your project metadata from the spreadsheet into R 

--Create a folder called "class_project" in your code folder 

--Save this file to the "class_project" folder 

--Move your Nexis spreadsheet to the folder 

--Create a project file on R Studio: File \| New Project \| \*\*\* select Existing folder \| "class_project" 

--After project.Rproj launches, then launch this file, metadata.Rmd, and complete the tutorial

**By doing this, you avoid the ring of hell where R can't find your data**

#load tidyverse, janitor, rio

```{r}

library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(rio)
#install.packages("readxl")
library(readxl)

```

#Import your data

```{r}

data <- read_excel("Base.XLSX")
View(data)

```

# Clean names

```{r}
data <- data |> 
  clean_names()

```

# check data types
```{r}
glimpse(data)
```


Next Steps: Count years, and create a ggplot

# Transform date into years. See tutorial
```{r}

data <- data |> 
  mutate(year = year(published_date))

```

```{r}
data |> 
  count(`countries`) |>
  arrange(desc(n))
```
```{r}
data |> 
  filter(length > 9000)
```

# counting
```{r}
data_big <- data |>
  mutate(length1 = as.numeric(length)) |>
  filter(length1 >=505)
```


# Create a ggplot
```{r}
data |> 
  count(year) |> 
   ggplot(aes(x = year, y = n,
             fill = n)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") + 
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  #scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(2015:2026)) + #fixes wonky x axis
  labs(title = "Dmitry Medvedev Performing on Nuclear Threat",
       subtitle = "Limited NexisUni Run",
       caption = "Graphic by Daria Davydova, 9-16-2026",
       y="Number of Articles",
       x="Year")



```

#Count publications

```{r}
data |> 
  count(`publication_4`)
```


#Visualize publications

```{r}
data |> 
count(publication_4) |> 
   ggplot(aes(x = publication_4, y = n,
             fill = n)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") + 
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle=90, hjust = 1))
  #scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(2022:2026)) + #fixes wonky x axis
  labs(title = "Dmitry Medvedev Performing on Nuclear Threat",
       subtitle = "Limited NexisUni Run",
       caption = "Graphic by Daria Davydova, 9-16-2026",
       y="Number of Articles",
       x="Publications")
```




# NOTES ON FIXING COMPLEX Date COLUMN WITH HOURS AND MINUTES

```{r}
women <- women |> 
  mutate(date = as.Date(strptime(published_date, format = "%B %d, %Y %A")))
```
